title: Part
spec: To construct a rectangular base, start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. The sketch consists of a single loop made up of four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.1302). The third line starts at (0.75, 0.1302) and ends at (0.0, 0.1302). Finally, the fourth line completes the loop by starting at (0.0, 0.1302) and ending at the origin (0.0, 0.0). After drawing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch. Ensure that the sketch remains aligned with the original coordinate system by rotating it using Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and translating it using a vector set to zero. To transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into a three-dimensional model, extrude the sketch 0.0098 units along the normal direction. Do not extrude in the opposite direction. This operation will create a new solid body with final dimensions of 0.75 units in length, 0.1302 units in width, and 0.0098 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.1302) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.1302) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a 3D object
r = r.extrude(0.0098)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0).lineTo(0.75, 0.1302).lineTo(0, 0.1302).close()

# Extrude the sketch
extrusion = sketch.extrude(0.0098)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation (if needed)
# In this case, the coordinate system is the default (0, 0, 0) with no rotation, so no transformation is needed.

# Final model
r = extrusion
